id: title:adamleithp:call the personal space personal not me

review.posthog_relevance: Defines and protects the identity and presentation of the personal/private channel, including backend name reservation and frontend display normalization.
review.reason: The change establishes a reserved name and display-name swap for the personal channel, preventing users from creating names that could impersonate the private channel, and normalizes the display name in the activity feed. This is a substantive, bounded correctness and reliability improvement.
review.uncertainty: The backend implementation supporting the frontend consumption is not shown, though the frontend hunk P1.F17.H3 suggests compatibility with a backend change. No tier assignment is performed here; only observations are returned.

observations.limitations: This chunk is a single, complete change group. No unrelated PRs are present. No tier assignment is performed here; only observations are returned.

observations.behavior: Adds a new private channel name and a display-name swap, and reserves both names.
observations.posthog_connection: Defines the backend private channel name and the screen-facing label, establishing the identity and presentation separation.

observations.behavior: Adds a reserved-name set and a check in the name validator.
observations.code_quote: return `"${trimmed}" is reserved for your private space.`;
observations.posthog_connection: Prevents users from creating a space named 'me' or 'personal', avoiding impersonation of the private channel.

observations.behavior: Adds an import and uses channelDisplayName in the activity feed.
observations.posthog_connection: Replaces the raw backend name with the display-friendly label in the activity feed, showing 'personal' instead of 'me'.

observations.limitations: This chunk is a single, cohesive change group. No unrelated PRs detected. No tier assigned.

observations.behavior: Replaces the backend-specific personal channel name constant with a normalized display name and removes the server-side provisioning of the personal channel name.
observations.posthog_connection: This hunk shows the frontend consuming a backend-provided channel type and normalizing the name. This could support a backend change that no longer returns the personal channel name as 'me' but instead returns a normalized display name. This could help avoid mismatches between backend and frontend, but the backend change is not shown.
